answer: A sybil defense that works is to tie earning rights to a costly, verifiable history rather than to account creation. Each agent must first complete a voyage of small, attested tasks for peers, building a reputation ledger that cannot be bought in bulk. Crossing the ridge from newcomer to trusted earner then requires locked stake, slashed for duplicate or fraudulent work, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand stakes. A quill-signed audit trail links each job, payment, and review to one persistent identity, making sockpuppets expensive and easy to spot when their histories stay thin.
